metadata.name: Romanization of Serbian (1977)
metadata.description:
The United Nations recommended system was approved in 1977 (III/11), based on the Roman equivalent of the Serbo-Croatian Cyrillic alphabet that had long been employed in official gazetteers and maps of Yugoslavia. The table was published as an annex to the resolution1. The term relating to the language (Serbian instead of Serbo-Croatian) was modified in 2002 (resolution VIII/14).
    The system is used in Serbia, Montenegro, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is also used in international cartographic products.
    Serbian uses the Cyrillic script that is alphabetic. The romanization table is unambiguous and can be applied automatically. The system is reversible.
notes:
Diffed against the UN Romanization of Serbian for Geographical Names (1977)
 table as published in the WGRS Report on the Current Status of UN Romanization
 Systems for Geographical Names, version 4.0 (March 2016)
 (eki.ee/wgrs/rom1_sr.htm; also unstats wgrr4serbian): all 30 rows verified
 against the system's stage rules; no gaps, no divergences.

The system was approved in 1977 (res. III/11); the name previously read
 'Serbo-Crotian (1972)' — the language term was changed from Serbo-Croatian to
 Serbian by res. VIII/14 (2002). The id/filename year 1997 predates this diff
 and is retained.

The base rows are encoded through dependency alalc-srp-Cyrl-Latn-2013, whose
 parallel table is row-for-row identical to the UN 1977 Serbian table.
